report:
I brought A, B, and C into a shared process. Each of them named needs and concerns, I named mine openly and invited correction, and I sent all three of them one running list to argue with.

Where things stand. The group has agreed that the three of them decide and I do not, and that I cannot make legal decisions or move money. All three agree B should not have to mediate between A and C.

On use: A needs the trailer for weekend trips in the next few weeks, wants flexibility, and accepts a cap on weekends booked ahead, proposing two weekends per month, with upcoming trips booked before the cap applies. C needs it within the next few weeks for a home project, wants a turn soon, and will not give up weekends until the project dates are known. Both said weekdays may work for C's project but neither has confirmed. Neither has sent dates yet; both said they will. The weekend cap number is not final.

On storage: B would rather the trailer was not on her pad and feels awkward asking. The pad is rented, so any change there needs her landlord's approval, which she has not requested. All three say they have no second place to suggest. B will look at shared paid storage but cannot commit to a cost. A and C are open to comparing paid storage costs.

On money: storage, upkeep, and cost shares are unsettled. No one has named an amount. C says no share can be proposed until costs are known. I flagged this as the most likely thing to break the plan.

Two dates are on the list: a review at the end of next month to decide where the trailer lives, and bookings made a few days ahead on one shared calendar, with B asked before every pickup and drop-off and able to decline a time.

My own concerns, all stated to the group: unbooked wishes turn into a race, B's "for now" needed a review date, and unsettled shares are the main risk. The review date eased the second. The other two remain open. My next steps would be to collect actual dates from A and C, get a weekend cap number agreed, and have one paid-storage option costed out before the review.
